posts.text:
This week, I talked to the parents and grandparents about GTA 6. But today, I want to talk to the young men playing it. The men who have spent their entire lives being talked about rather than being talked to. These men have always heard the same story, that they are falling behind, that they’re in crisis. And now, that narrative is back at it again.

I don’t play video games myself, but I understand the process. You start the game, fail a mission, and try again. I’ve heard that in games like Elden Ring, you might fail a hundred times to the same boss. Then, when you finally beat the boss, there’s always another challenge to fail at until you figure it out.

Nobody is paying you. Nobody is grading you. You’re just putting in the work, studying the patterns and making adjustments until you finally succeed.

There’s a word for this: mastery. That’s the exact “fail till you succeed” mindset you need if you want to be successful in this life. 

The difference is that in a game, you can fail at 2 a.m. and no one sees you start over. In real life, there’s no reset button, and it’s scary to go after your goals when others can see if you fail. I understand why that feels intimidating. But failure never stopped you from saving Peach from Bowser’s castle. Every time you saw the game over screen, you picked up the controller again.

So to the young men out there gaming this week, go ahead and have a good time. Just do me one favor. Before the week is up, pick one thing in your real life, say it out loud to someone who will actually hold you to it, and go and beat that level.

🇺🇸 What if the Pentagon's biggest UFO secret isn't aliens, but technology it's been hiding from humanity?

Project Unity's Jay Anderson believes the U.S government may be using the UFO phenomenon as a smokescreen to conceal extraordinary breakthroughs in classified military technology.

Anti-gravity propulsion, exotic energy systems, and aircraft capable of manoeuvres that appear to defy physics.

Jay suspects some of these technologies may have been developed secretly for decades, while the public has been encouraged to believe the government is just as confused about UFOs as everyone else.

But what if the modern UFO disclosure movement isn't exposing the cover-up, but helping to protect it?

Jay points to the 2017 disclosure campaign, arguing that its portrayal of a government desperately searching for answers conveniently obscures decades of potentially classified research.

He doesn't dismiss non-human intelligence; in fact, he believes it may exist.

But he suspects the real deception is that genuine unexplained phenomena and secret human technology have been deliberately blurred together.

The question may no longer be whether the Pentagon knows what UFOs are, but how much of the technology it already possesses.

posts.text:
An 18-year-old Georgia boy whose mom was dying of cancer learned to cook from her bedside, just so his 7 brothers and sisters could still have dinner every night.

Then she passed away in August.

Now 2 MILLION strangers are helping him finish what she started 💔

His name is Joey Charney, he's 18, from Augusta, Georgia, and his mom Jennifer was a stay-at-home mom of EIGHT kids.

About 10 years ago she was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer. In 2017 the family celebrated because she was cancer-free. Then in 2019 it came back, stage 4.

As she got sicker, the kids had to start doing all the things mom always did. Joey raised his hand to do the cooking, for 9 to 11 people, most nights.

He barely knew how to cook, so his mom taught him from her bed. "She could just smell like, 'Oh, it's burning.' And she would sit here and yell at me from her bed. And I was like, 'I got it! I got it!'" 😂

He started filming his meals and posting them online, the good ones and the not-so-good ones. And people FELL IN LOVE with him.

In August, after a 10-year fight, Jennifer passed away.

Joey thought about giving up.

...but then something unexpected happened.

Joey's followers started doing what his mom used to do. 

They encouraged him, they sent him recipes, they gave him cooking advice. 

Soon, nearly TWO MILLION people became the voice in the kitchen telling him he's got this.

Joey says he misses everything about her, "but her cooking especially. I can't get her Parmesan chicken the same way." 😭

This week he was practicing on whole chickens for the biggest meal of the year, because this is the family's first Thanksgiving without her. 

...and Joey is the one making it, this time without his mom

What an incredible mom she must have been... to raise such an awesome son like that ❤️
